symptom: The merge after an IF whose branch holds a foreach LOOP landed inside the loop's box: LoopedActivity 950;200 320x160 spans x 790..1110, ExclusiveMerge 1070;200 spans 1050..1090, so the loop's outgoing line ran right to left into it. mx check: 0 errors.
cause: measureLoopStatement sized a loop as body + 2*LoopPadding while addLoopStatement builds body + 2*LoopPadding + iteratorSpace (a local 100); the IF's mergeX comes from the measured branch width, so it fell 100px short for every foreach loop at every nesting level. WHILE has no iterator column and no mismatch.
insight: The issue's cause was right in effect but not in mechanism: the builder's `+iteratorSpace` width is overwritten by fitContainerSize after the body is built, so the column reaches the final width through innerStartX instead. The measurer still has to include it, because the IF reads the measured width before the loop exists. A centre-to-centre layout invariant (merge.X >= loop.X) passed throughout, so the test compares box EDGES (merge.X - MergeSize/2 >= loop.X + Width/2); TestLayoutInvariants_NoBackwardMergeAndEndRightmost treats a LoopedActivity as ActivityWidth wide and could not see it.
